title: Man Arrested with Knife Near ‘Miami Vice ’85’ Set Starring Michael B. Jordan, NBC Reports
body:
A 23‑year‑old Brooklyn man was taken into custody on Friday night after police said he brandished a knife near the active filming location of “Miami Vice ’85,” the forthcoming crime‑action movie starring Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler. The arrest, made just after 11 p.m. in the Williamsburg neighborhood, adds a surprising twist to a production that has already drawn considerable attention for its high‑profile cast and nostalgic revival of the 1980s television series.

According to New York City Police Department officials, officers responding to a disturbance report encountered Alex Perez, a resident of the borough, who was allegedly holding a knife and refusing to comply with commands. Perez was detained on charges of criminal possession of a weapon, reckless endangerment and resisting arrest. He was later processed at the 84th Precinct and is expected to appear in court later this month. Police did not disclose whether any injuries occurred, but witnesses said the situation was quickly contained and did not interfere with the film crew’s schedule.

The incident unfolded on a set that has been operating in Williamsburg for the past several weeks. “Miami Vice ’85” is a stylized prequel that transports the iconic Miami‑based detectives back to 1985, blending neon‑lit aesthetics with contemporary storytelling. Production, overseen by director Anthony Mann and producers Michael B. Jordan and his company Outlier Society, has been a magnet for onlookers, with crowds gathering daily to catch glimpses of the stars and elaborate set pieces. The presence of a knife‑wielding individual raised concerns not only for the safety of the cast and crew but also for the broader community, which has been navigating the challenges of a bustling film shoot in a densely populated urban area.

Law enforcement officials emphasized that the arrest was part of a routine response to a reported threat. “When we receive a call about an individual with a weapon, we treat it with the utmost seriousness, regardless of the location,” said NYPD spokesperson Lieutenant Maria Gonzalez. She added that officers arrived on scene within minutes and successfully de‑escalated the situation without further incident. The department’s swift action underscores the heightened security protocols that have become standard on major film sets, especially those involving high‑profile talent and large equipment rigs.

Industry insiders note that disruptions of this nature, while rare, can have ripple effects on production timelines and budgets. “Any unexpected security issue forces the crew to halt shooting, which can cost thousands of dollars per hour,” explained veteran line producer Carla Mendoza, who has worked on several New York‑based features. However, she also pointed out that the production team appears to have a contingency plan in place. “The crew has already resumed filming after a brief pause, and there’s no indication that the incident will cause a significant delay,” Mendoza said. The film’s producers have not released an official statement regarding the arrest, but sources close to the project indicated that they remain focused on completing the shoot ahead of its slated release next summer.

The episode also shines a light on the broader conversation about public safety in neighborhoods that host large‑scale entertainment projects. Williamsburg, once an industrial hub, has transformed into a cultural hotspot, attracting filmmakers, musicians and tourists alike. While the influx brings economic benefits, it also raises concerns about traffic congestion, noise and occasional confrontations between residents and production crews. City officials have been working with the Mayor’s Office of Film, Theatre and Broadcasting to develop clearer guidelines for managing these interactions, aiming to balance creative activity with community welfare.

As “Miami Vice ’85” moves toward post‑production, the focus will likely shift back to its artistic ambitions rather than the brief brush with law enforcement. The film is poised to capitalize on the chemistry between Jordan and Butler, promising a fresh take on a beloved franchise that could resonate with both nostalgic fans and new audiences. Meanwhile, the legal process for Alex Perez will continue, serving as a reminder that even in the glitter of Hollywood’s revival, ordinary civic responsibilities and public safety remain paramount.
